notes: Step 1 parts are unchanged: Arduino Uno, breadboard, potentiometer, red LED, 220 ohm resistor and five jumper wires.
Hole names follow the image's row labels: the lower half (rows a-e) is bank 't' and the upper half (rows f-j) is bank 'b'.
The tutorial text says the 5V and ground pins go to the pot's outer legs and the centre pin goes to A0. The pot is wired that way: wire1 (5V) to VCC, wire2 (GND) to GND, wire3 (A0) to SIG.

In the image the yellow A0 wire ends on the far side of the centre gap from the pot's legs. I put it in the same column strip as the pot's centre leg (23t) so that it is electrically connected, as the text and schematic require.
The resistor is placed in row g, from column 3 to column 6, so the blue pin 9 wire (3b.f) reaches its first lead. Its other lead shares column 6 with the LED anode.
LED polarity follows the tutorial: the anode (the bent, longer leg) is at the resistor's output, and the cathode goes to GND through the black wire at column 8.
The Uno has three GND pins. wire5 uses GND.1, which is on the digital header next to AREF. wire2 uses GND.2, which is on the power header.
